name: blur-fade
title: Blur Fade
description: A wrapper that eases content in from a blurred, offset ghost to full focus, optionally waiting until it scrolls into view. Here a heading, a line of copy and eight photos stagger into focus, plus a Replay button.
use: Content should arrive gently rather than pop in, such as photo grids, page intros or feature blocks.
avoid: Long lists or text people need at once, since each item starts blurred and unreadable until it plays.
a11y: Wrapped content starts invisible and blurred, and the code does not check reduced-motion preferences. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark section with a bold white heading and a small grey subtitle. Under them a four-column grid of eight square landscape photos with rounded corners, and a small outlined pill button labelled Replay beneath.
behaves: On entry each child rises a few pixels from a ghosted, blurred state to full sharpness after a short staggered pause, taking about half a second. Pressing Replay remounts the group so the whole reveal plays again.
customise: Anything can be wrapped as children; duration, delay, travel distance, direction, blur amount and the in-view trigger are props, plus a variants override for custom motion.
weight: light: One short opacity and blur transition per child; an intersection observer until it fires.
demo: Heading "Summer in the mountains", a subtitle about eight road frames, eight landscape photos, and a Replay button
issues: Pressing Replay blanks the whole section for a moment before it fades back in.
polishWhy: The staggered focus pull reads well and lands sharp; the blank beat on replay is a blemish.
